Class ReplicaBody

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.server.ReplicaBody
public final class ReplicaBody extends Object
A fake player run as if it had a game client of its own. The network learned on a real client, so a body without one is given everything a client would have made of the same keys. Each tick goes the way a client's does, in the same order:
  1. The opponent is where a client would show it (RemoteView), not where the server has it.
  2. The picture is the frame a client would have drawn last: part-way through the tick before, from where the body and the camera were then (SyntheticEye).
  3. The camera turns, and a click is judged straight away with the new view, against the opponent as shown, before the body moves.
  4. Then the keys move the body, and sprinting is kept the way a client keeps it and the server hears of it (ClientSprint).

sense(ServerPlayer, ServerPlayer, double) is the first two steps and act(ServerPlayer, ServerPlayer, int[], float, float) the last two; whoever decides in between (a trained network that only plays, or one that is learning) is not this class's business.

Used by the server thread only.

  • Method Details

    • setLag

      public void setLag(int ticks)
      How many ticks late this body gets to see its opponent, on top of what a client's own smoothing adds: none in a singleplayer world, a few on a server. Everything it does goes by the opponent as it sees it, a click included, exactly as for a real client.

    • setLag

      public void setLag(int ticks, float stallChance, int stallTicks)
      The same, over a connection that also stutters: on each tick there is this chance that nothing of the opponent arrives for one to stallTicks ticks, and then all of it at once. It is then seen standing still and jumping on, as a lagging player is.

    • click

      private void click(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer body, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer opponent)
      A left click, as a client resolves it: whatever is under the crosshair decides. The opponent within reach is hit; empty air is a miss and the weapon's charge starts over; a block in the way swallows the click, and then only the server starts the charge over (the client never notices, which is the game's own quirk and is kept).
